item.text: {"question_id":"6B.9","answer":"During the defined 2023 period, the evidence supports substantial institutional layering rather than demonstrated durability beyond personal rule. Standing disability law supplied statutory authority, required inclusion in plans and budgets, and contemplated stable fiscal support and administrative coordination; 2023 education and affordable-housing systems had substantial public funding, earmarking, monitoring, reporting, and performance-management rules. Health-insurance administration operated at national scale, with reported fund reserves, extensive inspections, recovered funds, medical assistance, and long-term-care-insurance pilots involving formal funds, service institutions, and care personnel. The long-term-care system also has pre-2023 policy roots and quasi-experimental evidence of reduced multidimensional poverty in earlier periods. These records show institutional continuity, funding mechanisms, administrative staffing requirements, and some professional or transparent standards, but they do not establish reliable long-term financing, independent professional autonomy, consistently transparent operation, or post-leadership resilience. Several 2023 reforms—including childcare standards, the minors-online regulation, and expanded administrative reconsideration—were enacted or promulgated in 2023 but became effective in 2024, so they demonstrate prospective statutory capacity, not observed 2023 implementation or durability. The contrary evidence is material: rural social-service incorporation and project termination may undermine NGO autonomy; disability-service organizations and advocacy channels were substantially government- and Party-controlled, with restrictions, shutdowns, limited participation, and unstable alternative funding; and top-down governance could suppress professional and bottom-up information. Local hidden debt and financial-management weaknesses further qualify funding reliability. The evidence therefore supports durable administrative and statutory layering in several welfare domains, with meaningful 2023 continuity and some inherited institutional performance, but leaves resilience beyond Xi-era centralized political authority
